To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the feedback inhibition of HMG-CoA-reductase by cholesterol occurs at the level of protein degradation.
dietary cholesterol reduces HMG-CoA-reductase mRNA levels, but not enzyme activity, and that dietary cholesterol reduces farnesyl-pyrophosphate synthetases activity, but not enzyme levels.
cholesterol-mediated feedback regulation of hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis is not mediated by altered mRNA levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis.

the regulation of cholesterol synthesis in the liver, which is controlled by a complex series of events that include the regulation of enzyme activity, mRNA levels, and the binding of nuclear proteins to the promoters of these genes.
the regulation of hepatic gene expression in response to dietary sterol and mevalonate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cholesterol-mediated regulation of HMG-CoA and farnesoyl pyrophosphate synthase activity is not at the transcriptional level but at the translational level.
dietary cholesterol decreases HMG-CoA synthase activity by decreasing mRNA levels and HMG-CoA activity by decreasing mRNA and protein levels.
dietary cholesterol and mevalolactone have no effect on HMG-CoA synthase, HMG-CoA lyase, and farnesoyl pyrophosphate synthase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary cholesterol and mevalonic acid decrease HMG CoA reductase by a post-transcriptional mechanism.
dietary cholesterol and mevalolactone have little effect on HMG-CoA mRNA levels but do have a profound effect on HMGCoA activity.
dietary cholesterol regulates hepatic cholesterol 7 alpha- hydroxylase and HMG-CoA synthase mRNA levels but not reductase mRNA levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional regulation of HMG-CoA synthase is not the main mechanism of cholesterol-mediated feedback regulation of HMGCoA reductases.
dietary cholesterol does not regulate hepatic HMG CoA reductase by changing mRNA levels.
cholesterol-mediated feedback inhibition of HMG-CoA is not mediated by changes in the transcription of the HMG-Coa reductase gene.
